technical-data.invention-title: COMPOSITIONS PHOTOSTABLES DE PROTECTION CONTRE LES ULTRAVIOLETS

abstract.p: The present invention relates to photostable compositions suitable for providing protection against the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation. The compositions provide excellent efficiency and broad spectrum UV efficacy while exhibiting improved photostability. Methods of use for these compositions are also disclosed. The present compositions comprise: a) an effective amount of a UVA-absorbing dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active; b) a photostabilizing system consisting essentially of an effective amount of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycinnamate; and c) a suitable carrier; wherein the mole ratio of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycinnamate to the dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active is from about 0.15:1 to about 1:1.

L'invention concerne des compositions photostables de protection contre les effets nocifs des rayons ultraviolets. Ces compositions sont extrêmement efficaces, possèdent un large spectre d'efficacité contre les ultraviolets, tout en présentant une photostabilité améliorée. Elle concerne également des procédés d'utilisation de ces compositions. Ces dernières contiennent: (a) une quantité efficace d'un écran solaire actif de dibenzoylméthane absorbant les ultraviolets; (b) un système photostabilisant constitué essentiellement par une quantité efficace de 2-éthylhexyl-p-méthoxycinnamate; (c) un véhicule adéquat; le rapport molaire entre 2-éthylhexyl-p-méthoxycinnamate et l'écran solaire actif de dibenzoylméthane étant situé entre 0,15:1 et 1:1.

description.p: PHOTOSTABLE UV PROTECTION COMPOSITIONS

TECHNICAL FIELD The present invention relates to photostable compositions suitable for providmg protection against the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation wherem the compositions have excellent efficiency and broad spectrum UV efficacy The compositions which exhibit improved and unexpected photostabihty comprise a UVA-absorbmg dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active, a photostabilizing system containing 2-ethylhexyl-p- methoxycinnamate and a suitable carrier such that the mole ratio of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxvcιnnamate to UVA-absorbmg dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active is from about 0 15 1 to about 1 1
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

It is well known that exposure to sunlight can pose a number of hazards to the skin These damaging effects may result not only from sunbathing but also from the sunlight exposure associated with daily outdoor activities The major short term hazard of prolonged exposure to sunlight is erythema, I e , sunburn, which primarily results from UVB radiation having a wavelength of from about 290 n to about 320 nm Over the long term, however, malignant changes in the skin surface often occur Numerous epideminologic studies demonstrate a strong relationship between sunlight exposure and human skin cancer Another long term hazard of ultraviolet radiation is premature agmg of the skin, which is primarily caused by UVA radiation havmg a wavelength of from about 320 nm to about 400 nm This condition is characterized by wrinkling and pigment changes of the skm, along with other physical changes such as crackmg, telangiectasis, solar dermatoses, ecchymoses, and loss of elasticity The adverse effects associated with exposure to UV radiation are more fully discussed in DeSimone, "Sunscreen and Suntan Products," Handbook of Nonprescrψtion Drugs, 7th Ed , Chapter 26, pp 499-511 (American Pharmaceutical Association, Washington, D C , 1982), Grove and Forbes, "A Method for Evaluating the Photoprotection Action of Sunscreen Agents Against UV-A Radiation," International Journal of Cosmetic Science, 4, pp 15-24 (1982)

As a result of the abovementioned hazards associated with sunlight exposure, the general public's interest m the sun protection product market has grown considerably Today, there are not only sunscreen products for sunbathing but there are also a variety of personal care products containing sunscreens, particularly cosmetic type products which are worn daily "Personal care products" refer to health and cosmetic beauty aid products generally recognized as being formulated for beautifying and grooming the skin and hair For example, personal care products mclude sunscreen products (e g., lotions, skm creams, etc.), cosmetics, toiletries, and over-the-counter pharmaceutical products intended for topical usage
Many conventional sunscreen products, m particular, are deficient, however, due to their inability to provide efficacious protection against broad spectrum UV radiation, 1 e , protection against both UVB and UVA radiation Today, most commercially available sunscreen products are efficient at absorbing UV radiation in the 290 nm to 320 nm UVB region such that sunburn of the skin is prevented They are less efficient when it comes to absorbing light which falls in the 320 nm to 400 nm UVA region, which leaves the skin vulnerable to premature skin aging This deficiency is due in part to the limited number of UVA absorbing sunscreen actives which are both commercially available and approved for global use One class of these sunscreen actives includes dibenzoylmethane compounds which provide broad spectrum UV protection and are described in U S Patent Nos 4 387,089, issued to De Polo on June 7, 1983 and 4,489,057, issued to Welters et al on December 18, 1984 4-tert-butyl-4'-methoxydιbenzoylmethane, m particular, is approved for global use Unfortunately, when used individually in sunscreen products, most dibenzoylmethane compounds tend to photodegrade upon exposure to UV radiation thereby reducing their UVA efficacy Furthermore, it is well known that even when dibenzoylmethane compounds are used in combination with other sunscreen actives, severe photodegradation still tends to occur For instance, U S Patent No 4,387,089 proposes to combine 4-(l,l dιmethylethyl)-4'-methoxydιbenzoylmethane with various UVB sunscreen actives, namely 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycιnnamate (also referred to as octyl methoxycinnamate), for the purpose of absorbmg all of the UV radiation between 280 and 380 nm and in which case it is stated that the ratio of the dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active to the UVB sunscreen active is not critical In fact, it is well known that the combination of 4-tert-buty 1-4' -methoxy dibenzoylmethane and 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycmnamate results m a formulation m which both of the sunscreen actives are photounstable which in turn makes the overall formulation photounstable Without being limited by theory, it is believed that upon exposure to UV radiation, 4-tert-butyl-4'-methoxydιbenzoylmethane and 2- ethylhexyl-p-methoxycinnamate react with each other to form non-UV absorbing compounds

Therefore sunscreen pioducts which include dibenzoylmethane sunscreen actives are typically more difficult to lormulate due to their inherent lack of photostabihty One approach to stabilize these types of sunscreens is described in U S Patent No 5,783,174 issued to Deckner on July 21, 1998, which involves the use of benzyhdene camphor sunscreens to stabilize the dibenzoylmethane compound Such compositions, however, are not currently approved for global use on humans

Thus, there is a need for photostable compositions suitable for providing protection against the harmful effects of UV radiation to human skm In particular, in the personal care industry, a need remams for sunscreen products having excellent photostabihty, efficiency, and which provide broad spectrum UV protection (I e , against both UVA and UVB radiation) m a safe and economical manner

Likewise, m other industries such as the automotive care, marine vehicle care, household care, animal care, and coatmgs industries, UV radiation causes undesirable wear and damage Therefore, a need exists for photostable compositions suitable for providing protection against the harmful elfects of UV radiation to a variety of objects and/or mateπals prone to sun exposure

In contrast to the common knowledge of those having ordinary skill in the art, Applicant has surprisingly found that the compositions of the present invention, which comprise a UVA-absorbmg
dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active, a photostabilizing system which includes 2-ethylhexyl-p- methoxycinnamate, and a suitable carrier such that the mole ratio of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycιnnamate to UVA-absorbing dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active is from about 0 15 1 to about 1 1, provide excellent photostabihty, efficiency, and UV protection efficacy (including both UVA and UVB protection), in a safe and economical manner
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a photostable composition suitable for providing protection against the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation comprising a) an effective amount of a UVA-absorbmg dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active, b) a photostabilizing system consisting essentially of an effective amount of 2-ethylhexyl-p- methoxycinnamate, and c) a suitable carrier, wherein the mole ratio of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycmnamate to the dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active is from about 0 15 1 to about 1 1

In preferred embodiments, the UVA-absorbing dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active and 2-ethylhexyl-p- methoxycinnamate are present m "safe and effective" amounts and the mole ratio of 2-ethylhexyl-p- methoxycinnamate to UVA-absorbing dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active is preferably from about 0 3 1 to about 0 9 1, more preferably from about 0 45 1 to about 0 8 1, even still more preferably from about 0 6 1 to about 0 75 1, and most preferably from about 0 65 1 to about 0 75 1 The present invention also relates to methods for providing protection to skm from the harmful effects of UV radiation by topical application of such compositions Furthermore, the present invention relates to methods of stabilizing a composition which comprises a UVA-absorbmg dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active and 2 ethylhexyl-p- methoxycmnamate
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

The compositions of the present invention are useful for providing photostable protection against the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation especially to human skm The essential components of these compositions are described below Also included is a nonexclusive description of various optional and preferred components useful in embodiments of the present invention
The present invention can comprise, consist of, or consist essentially of any of the required or optional ingredients and/or limitations described herein

All percentages and ratios are calculated on a weight basis unless otherwise indicated All percentages are calculated based upon the total composition unless otherwise indicated All molar weights are weight average molecular weights and are given in units of grams per mole
All ingredient levels are in reference to the active level of that ingredient, and are exclusive of solvents, by-products, or other impurities that may be present in commercially available sources, unless otherwise indicated
All measurements made are at ambient room temperature, which is approximately 73°F. unless otherwise designated
All documents referred to herein, including patents, patent applications, and printed publications, are hereby incorporated by reference in their entirety in this disclosure

Photostabilizing System

The compositions of the present invention also comprise a photostabilizing system which consists essentially of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycιnnamate The photostabilizing system is useful for reducing the photodegradation, I e , the photoinstabihty, of the UVA-absorbing dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active as well as the photodegration of the composition of the present invention Photodegradation may be
determined by a reduction of the UV absorption capability which in turn may be measured by usmg standard UV absorbance methods. Preferred compositions retain at least about 75%, more preferably at least about 85%, and most preferably at least about 95%, of their initial UV absorption after irradiation with approximately 2 J/cm: per desired SPF unit of broad band UV radiation, e.g., 30 J/cnr for an SPF 15 composition. The 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycιnnamate is present in the photostabilizing system m an amount such that the mole ratio of 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycιnnamate to UVA-absorbing dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active is from about 0.15: 1 to about 1.1. preferably from about 0.3: 1 to about 0.9: 1 , more preferably from about 0.45: 1 to about 0.8: 1, even more preferably from about 0.6: 1 to about 0.75: 1, and most preferably from about 0.65: 1 to about 0.75: 1

Preferably, the carriers of the present invention are suitable for application to skm (e.g., sunscreens, creams, milks, lotions, masks, serums, etc.); hair and fur (e.g., shampoos, hair setting or treatment gels or lotions, shapmg/curhng/fixation lacquers or lotions, etc.); and nails (e.g., polishes, treatments, etc.). In preferred embodiments, the carrier is suitable for application to skm which means that the carrier and its components are suitable for use in contact with skm, hair, fur, and nails without undue toxicity. incompatibility, instability, allergic response, and the like withm the scope of sound medical judgment. Such carriers are well-known to one of ordinary skill in the art, and can include one or more compatible liquid or solid filler diluents or vehicles which are suitable for application to skm. hair, fur, and nails. The exact amount of carrier will depend upon the level of the UVA-absorbmg dibenzoylmethane sunscreen active, the 2-ethylhexyl-p-methoxycmnamate and any other optional ingredients which one of ordinary skill in the art would classify as distinct from the carrier (e.g., other active components) The compositions of the present invention preferably comprise from about 20% to about 99 8%, more preferably from about 50% to about 99%, and most preferably from 75% to about 95%, by weight of the composition, of a carrier.

Any additional components required to formulate such products vary with product type and can be routmely chosen by one skilled in the art.

Methods For Providing Protection From UV Radiation

The compositions of the present invention are suitable for providing protection against the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation, preferably in personal care products More preferably, the compositions of the present invention are suitable for use as sunscreens to provide protection to human skin from the harmful effects of UV radiation which include, but are not limited to, sunburn and premature aging of the skm The present invention therefore also further relates to methods of protecting human skm from the harmful effects of UV radiation Such methods generally involve attenuating or reducing the amount of UV radiation which reaches the skm's surface To protect the skm from UV radiation, a safe and effective (photoprotective) amount of the composition is topically applied to the skm "Topical application" refers to application of the present compositions by spreading, spraying, etc onto the surface of the skm The exact amount applied may vary depending on the level of UV protection desired Fiom about 0 5 mg of composition per cm2 of skm to about 25 mg of composition per cm2 of skm are typically applied
